title: A Reproducible Data-Processing and Evaluation Framework for Federated Agricultural Knowledge Repositories
content:
Agricultural catalogues are awkward to benchmark once the records stay at the centres that produced them. We turn 75,897 bibliographic records from the International System for Agricultural Science and Technology (AGRIS), already held by 7 area-prefix clients, into a federated multi-view benchmark. Each record has four disjoint views (1,096 features), a ten
class AGROVOCheuristic, publication-level grouping, a client- and class-aware 70/10/20 cut, and ablinded400-record subject-matter expert (SME) audit. Against the consensus gold the heuristic reached 94.50% accuracy and macro-F1 = 0.945 (sampling-weighted 94.91%). 
Grouping removes 1,132 duplicate-document groups that would otherwise cross folds. Compute-matched Federated Averaging (FedAvg) is 0.2998 ± 0.0151 macro-F1, against 0.3041 ± 0.0021 when the data are pooled and 0.2884 ± 0.0037 when they are not. Eight-bit uplink quantization keeps 0.3001 ± 0.0147 at a 4× uplink cut (1.6× on total traffic). The full pipeline is archived on Zenodo as release v1.0 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22956341). This is a benchmark and evaluation framework, not a new federated-learning method.
